title: Elric and the Goblin's Shiny Surprise
markdown:
High up on the rocky sun-warmed tops of Sunspike Peaks, where the wind sang soft songs and sometimes grumbled like a sleepy giant, lived a young wizard named Elric. Elric wasn’t like the wizards in old storybooks. His spells often went fizz instead of flash, and his best friend was a raven named Corvus. Corvus was as black as a moonless night, with eyes that sparkled like shiny black beads. He had a way of tilting his head, as if he understood more than any bird should. When the sun shone on his feathers they gleamed with hints of deep purple and bright green, like tiny hidden jewels. Elric’s tower room was warm and smelled of dried lavender, bubbling potions, and old paper. Sunlight peeked through tall windows, making dust motes dance like tiny lazy fairies.

One breezy morning, as Elric polished his crystal ball—which mostly showed puffy clouds that looked a lot like sheep—he remembered something. A small important task.

“Ah, Corvus, my feathered friend. I borrowed a special charm from Old Man Hemlock. A Moonpetal Charm, a gentle thing that glows with soft light. It needs to go back to the Whispering Woods, to a cave that hums with quiet tunes. It must be returned before the next full moon, or its song might fade away forever.”

Corvus ruffled his smooth feathers, looking very important. A sharp smart Caw! To Elric it sounded like: about time, slowpoke. Ready for an adventure.

So, with a worn leather bag slung over his shoulder, the glowing Moonpetal Charm wrapped in soft moss, Elric and Corvus set off. The path down from the peaks was a winding ribbon of grey stone dotted with tough mountain flowers. The wind, a playful friend, tugged at Elric’s robes, making them flap like flags. It whispered secrets of old rocks and wild creatures that Elric almost understood.

As they stepped into the cool shady part of the ancient trees, the air grew cooler. Rich and earthy: damp soil, fallen leaves, sweet hidden flowers. Elric, being a careful wizard, pulled out a crinkly map, edges soft from being folded many times. The lines wiggled like the roots of giant trees. Corvus was not a map-lover. Maps were too plain for a clever raven. He soared ahead, a dark blur against bright green leaves, cawing happily as he chased shimmering dragonflies that zipped by like tiny flying jewels.

“Corvus, wait! We must follow the path! The Whispering Woods can trick you if you’re not careful!”

But Corvus, with a mischievous glint, swooped down very fast and snatched a bright shiny button that had fallen from a traveller’s coat. With a triumphant caw that bounced through the trees, he flew to a low branch and started pecking at the button, trying to make it sing like a tiny metal bird.

“Corvus, that’s not a treasure for a wizard’s raven.” Elric sighed, but a smile tugged at his lips. He knew Corvus loved shiny things as much as he loved his glossy feathers. “The charm needs to go back to its special cave. And besides, buttons don’t usually sing, do they?”

Corvus, not minding the gentle scolding, dropped the button. He hopped closer, nudging Elric’s bag with his beak, quite proud of himself for being so brave and getting the shiny thing, as if he’d battled a dragon. He even puffed out his chest a little, hoping for a compliment.

They walked deeper. Trees grew taller and more majestic, branches like old wrinkly fingers reaching for the sky. Light grew softer, golden beams through leaves. Suddenly a gruff voice startled them, pebbles rattling in a tin can.

“Stop! Who’s there, bothering my collection?”

Peeking from behind a big gnarled oak, bark like wrinkled old skin, was a goblin no taller than Elric’s knee. A long pointy nose that sniffed the air. Ears that twitched at every sound. An amazing collection of odd things: a chipped teacup sat crookedly on his head, a single bright glove on his left hand, a smooth shiny pebble balanced on the tip of his nose. The goblin collector. Eyes sharp and beady like a robin’s, darting everywhere.

“Hello, sir.” Elric bowed politely. Politeness was a good spell. “I’m Elric, and this is my raven, Corvus. We’re looking for a cave that hums with a quiet tune, to return a borrowed charm.”

The goblin’s sharp eyes landed on Corvus’s shiny black feathers, then flicked to Elric’s bag, where the soft glow of the Moonpetal Charm peeked out. “Humming, you say? How interesting. A cave that sings! But what have we here?” A grubby quick finger pointed at Corvus. “A creature so wonderfully shiny! And your bag, young wizard, what sparkles inside? Starlight? Captured moonbeams?”

“Just a charm. It’s for returning, not for keeping. It belongs to someone who really likes its soft glow.”

Corvus, sensing the goblin liked all things shiny, puffed out his chest and stepped closer. He rather enjoyed the attention. A loud proud Caw! Caw! He ruffled his wings, making them gleam.

The goblin collector’s eyes grew wide as saucers. The pebble on his nose wobbled. He rummaged in his pockets, rustling and clinking, and pulled out a tiny tarnished silver bell, no bigger than Elric’s fingernail, shining faintly. “Aha! A sound of pure delight! A tiny bell that whispers of forgotten tunes! Perhaps we can trade?” He held it out to Corvus.

Corvus, who had a funny liking for anything that jingled, tilted his head. Black eyes fixed on the dancing silver. Then, with a quick skilful move that surprised even Elric, he snatched the bell from the goblin’s fingers. Caw! He flapped up to the branches. The tiny bell tinkled merrily, a shower of silver notes falling through the quiet woods.

The goblin stammered, mouth hanging open. “My prize! My prize! You feathered rascal! That bell was meant for my collection of wonderful sounds!”

Elric put a hand to his forehead, embarrassed and amused. “Oh, Corvus! You’ve made us look silly! That was a perfectly good bell you just… took!”

Then a most peculiar thing happened. After his shock, the goblin began to chuckle. A low rumble in his chest, like far-off thunder, growing into a wheezing happy laugh that shook his whole little body. He held his sides, tears of laughter streaming down wrinkled cheeks. “Hah! Amazing! I’ve never seen such boldness from a bird! He has more spirit than many knights I know, who would have just bowed and stuttered! That raven has a soul full of mischief!”

They did not rush the next minute. Elric stood in the leaf-gold and let the bell finish a phrase. Corvus conducted from the branch. The wind rustled above. The world held its breath, listening.

“That’s the curious thing about collections,” the goblin said, laughter quieting into a happy sigh. “Sometimes the most precious things are not the ones you catch, but the ones that get away.” He looked at Elric, real warmth, not gruffness. “The cave you seek is past the mossy stones, where the old willow tree weeps silvery leaves. And your raven… he has a certain flair. A collector of experiences, perhaps.”

Elric felt a wave of relief, like a gentle tide. “Thank you, sir. You are very kind. And perhaps Corvus could bring that bell back to you, after he’s finished with its magical tinkling?”

The goblin nodded, a real smile creasing his wrinkled face. “Perhaps he could. And if he finds any more shiny things that sing or sparkle, tell him Old Grolbin the collector is always interested. A creature with such good taste is rare indeed!”

And so, with a new understanding, a lighter bag—the Moonpetal Charm still safely tucked—and the cheerful tinkle of a silver bell guiding their steps, Elric and Corvus continued. They soon found the cave. Its entrance softly hummed a tune that only the wind and the Moonpetal Charm understood, a melody like the sigh of a contented dream. Elric placed the charm gently in its mossy spot. The humming grew deeper, a sound of perfect happiness and thanks. The cave itself seemed to glow a little brighter.

As they walked back toward the welcoming peaks of Sunspike, Corvus flew beside Elric. He occasionally jingled the silver bell, but mostly he was happy just to be near his wizard. The charm sang where it belonged. The button, left on the path, did not sing. Grolbin, somewhere behind them, was already listening for the next jingle.
characters: Elric (young wizard of Sunspike Peaks), Corvus (jewel-gleam raven)
